input.subject: RFC: adding pytest as a supported test framework

verdict_reasoning: The thread shows demand and the goal has support, so level 1b holds. The design leaves three things open that the list must settle before code review. It has no buildfarm plan for installing dependencies and collecting results (prior-attempts-1), no rule that keeps ported tests running where pytest is absent (standards-compat-2), and no end state for the two-framework period (maintenance-fit-1). [P4] shows a Python change reverted because the buildfarm was not ready.

brief.title: Add pytest as a supported test framework alongside Perl TAP tests
brief.problem: Developers cannot rerun one failing TAP test alone, and failure output rarely shows what failed without reading logs. Few newer contributors know Perl, so they avoid writing tests, and the Perl suite gives little room for modern tooling or for testing client and server separately, for example against a mock peer.
brief.proposed_design: Configure and Meson gain an option that runs Python test suites under pytest, with a custom plugin that turns pytest results into TAP output for the Meson test runner. A shared Python package adds fixtures that start and stop clusters, run queries through a ctypes binding to libpq, and map server errors to Python exceptions. Later patches port the load balance tests and parts of the SSL tests.
user_visible_surface: Configure option --enable-pytest and Meson option -Dpytest (feature, default auto).
Meson option PYTEST, the path to the pytest binary.
Meson option tap_tests description changed to say the TAP tests are Perl-based.
New test tree src/test/pytest with a shared Python fixtures package and a pgtap output plugin.
Python package dependencies: pytest, plus cryptography for the SSL tests.
author_claims: pytest fixtures let each test declare its own setup, so a single failing test can be rerun in isolation.
Plain assert statements show the compared values on failure, with no comparison DSL to learn.
Server logs are attached to the failure report, split by setup, test and teardown.
The Perl tests stay in place, and the pytest entry point can be reverted cleanly if it does not work out.
In-person meetings showed support or neutrality and no strong objections.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund wants central infrastructure first and a smaller first patch; Jelte cut the patch set down in v9 and has rebased it through v13. Jacob plans no fast-track and wants buy-in from several maintainers, and no committer has said they will commit it.
unclear: Plan and timeline for porting existing Perl TAP tests, now that the author says side-by-side forever was outvoted.
How packagers and buildfarm members install pytest and cryptography without a virtualenv, a concern Andres raised.
Whether the patch has replies to the objections raised by Tom Lane and Robert Haas about running two frameworks long term.
How the Autoconf path, which runs pytest directly, reports results to the buildfarm client.
Which minimum Python and pytest versions the project commits to supporting.

prior_attempts.title: Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test
prior_attempts.quote: I have reverted this because of the build farm issue. Putting the patch on hold in the CF until we have a new plan.
prior_attempts.reason: Peter Eisentraut committed the basic TAP test, then reverted it because of a build farm issue and set the entry to Returned with feedback until there was a new plan. Two points were also still open: the patch removed the documented cross-version upgrade testing, and there was no plan for build farm animals that call vcregress.pl upgradecheck.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 replaced one test script with a TAP test and was reverted over a build farm issue. This proposal adds a whole test framework, so the buildfarm readiness question is larger.

prior_attempts.title: Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test - take two
prior_attempts.quote: Basically, it imposes that from now on all program invocations must observe the bindir setting, which someone is surely going to forget.
prior_attempts.reason: A new TAP suite in the pg_upgrade directory would make the buildfarm client run the pg_upgrade tests twice, so a buildfarm client release was needed first, and the author judged the commitfest window too short for v11. Peter Eisentraut also found the PostgresNode.pm bindir refactoring too invasive, because every program call must now observe the bindir setting and future code can forget it. Cross-version runs still failed to load regress.so and related libraries after the upgrade.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 needed a buildfarm client release before a new TAP suite could land. This proposal adds a new suite type, and the thread names no client change.

objections.title: No stated plan for buildfarm client support of pytest suites
objections.failure_scenario: After commit, buildfarm animals where -Dpytest=auto finds pytest start running the new suites, while animals without it skip them without notice. Under Autoconf, pytest runs directly with colored output and no TAP or log file, so failures are not captured in a form the buildfarm client collects. Committers find out when failures appear that nobody can read.
objections.argument: Earlier test infrastructure changes were reverted or returned when the buildfarm was not ready: a new TAP suite for pg_upgrade [P1][P3], and configure's preference for python3 [P4]. Message #77 says the buildfarm client depends on test output being saved to files. Message #71 notes that a venv-only setup blocks packagers, and message #92 has the Autoconf path running pytest directly. The thread does not yet say how buildfarm owners install pytest and cryptography, or how the client reports pytest results.
objections.author_must_show: How will buildfarm animals install the dependencies and collect pytest results under both Meson and Autoconf, and does that need a client release before commit?

precedents.title: Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test
Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test - take two
Revert "Make configure prefer python3 to plain python."

critic.reasoning: No message through v13 says how buildfarm animals install pytest and cryptography or how the client collects pytest results, and message #77 says the client relies on stored log files. [P4] applies directly; [P1] and [P3] support only the point about buildfarm client readiness.

objections.title: Ported Perl tests disappear for builds without pytest
objections.failure_scenario: A packager builds with tap_tests enabled but has no pytest, which Andres expects in message #71, so -Dpytest=auto turns itself off. When the load balance TAP test is replaced by a Python version, that coverage is gone from the package build with no warning. A libpq load-balancing regression then passes their tests.
objections.argument: The brief and v9-0003 convert the load_balance_hosts Perl test to Python. Message #92 says the plan now includes porting Perl tests at some point. Because the option defaults to auto, a ported test becomes a test that silently does not run wherever pytest is missing. Back branches keep the Perl version, so the same fix needs a different test on each branch.
objections.author_must_show: Until pytest is required, what stops a ported test from silently losing coverage on builds where pytest is absent, and will the Perl version stay alongside it?

critic.reasoning: The `auto` default copies `tap_tests`, and v9 labels the load balance port a POC after message #108 asked not to remove an existing test. But message #92 expects ports later, and no message says the Perl version stays until pytest is required.

objections.title: Pinned pytest version range ties configure to upstream release dates
objections.failure_scenario: A distribution moves to a pytest release outside the declared range. With -Dpytest=auto, the pytest suites quietly stop running on that platform. With -Dpytest=enabled, configure fails on a stable branch that nobody has touched, and someone must backpatch a bump to the version range.
objections.argument: The v2 requirements file pins pytest to at least 7.0 and below 9, and it adds cryptography with a lower bound that follows Debian releases. The brief notes that the project has not said which minimum Python and pytest versions it supports. Message #42 asks that new dependencies be judged on a 10- to 20-year view, but the patch has no policy for when a range is widened, or on which branches.
objections.author_must_show: Which Python, pytest and cryptography versions will each supported branch accept, and who widens the range on old branches when distributions move ahead?

precedents.title: Revert "Make configure prefer python3 to plain python."

critic.reasoning: Message #101 replaced the v2 requirements file and check script with pyproject.toml and importorskip, so the configure failure may no longer happen as described. The thread still names no supported Python, pytest and cryptography versions per branch, so the version policy question stands.

objections.title: Two test frameworks with no stated migration plan
objections.failure_scenario: A committer changes server setup defaults or adds a helper in PostgreSQL::Test::Cluster. The pypg fixtures keep the old behaviour because no build step or test compares the two. Months later, the Perl and pytest suites disagree on the same feature, and a reviewer has to read both languages to find out why.
objections.argument: Tom Lane (message #42) and Robert Haas (messages #48, #68) objected to running two parallel frameworks with similar capabilities for ten to twenty years. Message #92 says side-by-side forever was outvoted, but no version up to v13 gives a porting plan, a timeline, or an end state. Without that, the patch commits the project to keeping two cluster-management layers in sync indefinitely. Message #55 notes that reverting test infrastructure once tests depend on it has rarely happened.
objections.author_must_show: Which Perl suites will be ported, in what order and by when, and what rule decides whether a new test goes in Perl or Python until then?

critic.reasoning: Robert Haas accepted the two-framework cost in principle in messages #55 and #68, which lowers the weight of this objection. But message #92 says ports are now expected, and no later version gives an order, an end state, or a rule for new tests.

refuted.title: Autoconf path runs pytest outside the TAP result format
refuted.failure_scenario: A buildfarm animal on an Autoconf build turns on --enable-pytest. make check runs pytest directly, so its results never pass through prove or the regress_log files. A pytest failure then shows up as a step failure with no per-test log that the buildfarm client can collect, and the owner finds out only when a red run arrives with nothing to read.
refuted.argument: Message #92 says the Autoconf path runs pytest directly, not through pgtap and prove, for a nicer developer view. In message #70 Tom Lane said he would vote -1 on Python tests that need their own result-collection setup, and in message #77 Andrew Dunstan called the stashed log files a feature the buildfarm needs. The Meson path solves this with the pgtap plugin, but the patch does not say how Autoconf output reaches the buildfarm client. [P3] and [P1] show that test-harness changes the buildfarm client did not expect have held back earlier proposals.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a buildfarm client on an Autoconf build collect pytest results and logs for each test, and does it need a client release first?

precedents.title: Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test - take two
Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which covers the Autoconf result collection and also the dependency installation.

refuted.title: Default auto option can silently drop ported coverage on buildfarm
refuted.failure_scenario: A buildfarm animal or a packager's build has no pytest or cryptography from the distribution, so -Dpytest=auto turns the suite off. Once the load balance tests exist only in Python, that platform stops running them, and nobody notices until a regression ships.
refuted.argument: Andres (message #71) said venv-only installation blocks packagers. The proposal still does not say how buildfarm members get pytest and cryptography, or which versions are supported; v2 pinned pytest below 9. Message #77 says the buildfarm client depends on per-test log files, and the Autoconf path runs pytest directly instead of emitting TAP. [P4] records a Python change reverted because the buildfarm was not ready.
refuted.author_must_show: How will buildfarm animals and packagers get supported pytest and cryptography versions, and what keeps a missing dependency from silently disabling tests that no longer exist in Perl?

precedents.title: Revert "Make configure prefer python3 to plain python."

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2 for the silent loss of ported coverage, and of prior-attempts-1 for the buildfarm dependencies.

refuted.title: Hand-written ctypes libpq binding needs manual syncing
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer adds a libpq function, an error code, or a type output change. The ctypes binding and its Python type parsing are not updated, and tests either cannot use the new behaviour or misparse results. The developer finds out only when someone writes a pytest that touches it.
refuted.argument: The patch adds a project-owned FFI layer to libpq, with error-to-exception mapping and conversion of results to Python types. Message #99 found array parsing that breaks on quoted and nested values and timestamp parsing that depends on DateStyle. Message #104 reports 32-bit loading problems. Nothing in the build checks this binding against libpq-fe.h or errcodes.txt, so drift goes unnoticed.
refuted.author_must_show: What keeps the ctypes binding and type conversion in step with libpq-fe.h, errcodes.txt and type output, and does the build fail when they drift?

critic.reasoning: A new libpq function that has no binding yet breaks nothing, because the test that first needs it adds the binding, and existing libpq signatures stay stable. Message #101 says the parsing problems from message #99 were addressed, and Robert Haas asked for a libpq FFI in message #52.

refuted.title: Most technical gains look reachable in the existing Perl TAP framework
refuted.failure_scenario: The project adds pytest while PostgreSQL::Test::Cluster, BackgroundPsql and a libpq FFI for Perl keep evolving. Two frameworks then grow in parallel, and each fixture or helper is written twice. Committers find this out when a backpatched test must be ported between languages or reviewed in both.
refuted.argument: Several stated problems have answers in the existing framework. Andrew proposed printing regress_log on failure and fixing ok() misuse with cmp_ok() or like() (message #77), and he posted a Perl libpq FFI proof of concept (messages #56, #69). Jelte agreed that only pytest's expression introspection is out of reach for Perl (message #78), and Robert called the rest a language popularity contest (message #79). The remaining case is per-test fixture isolation and contributor preference, and the proposal does not yet show that this justifies a second framework that people expect to replace Perl later (message #92).
refuted.author_must_show: Which concrete tests, such as mock-peer protocol tests, cannot be written with Test::More plus the Perl libpq FFI, and why can isolation not be added there?

critic.reasoning: Messages #3, #38, #43 and #87 show the need is common, and Perl improvements cannot fix contributors avoiding Perl. Robert Haas weighed this in messages #48 and #59 and found improving Perl alone unrealistic; [P8] rejected a Perl protocol client and does not apply.

refuted.title: Costs fall on all committers and buildfarm owners, with no plan to end them
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer pushes a fix whose only test is a pytest suite. With -Dpytest at its default of auto, buildfarm animals that lack pytest skip that suite without failing. A later regression in that code goes unseen on those platforms until a user reports it.
refuted.argument: The material shows real demand among developers: the unconference sessions, outside pytest suites, and messages #3, #38 and #87. The cost is broader than that group: every committer must review two frameworks, and buildfarm owners and packagers must install pytest and cryptography (message #71). Message #92 says permanent side-by-side was outvoted, but no porting plan or end date follows. The two-framework cost raised in messages #42 and #68 has no recorded answer in the thread.
refuted.author_must_show: What porting plan and timeline end the two-framework period, and how many buildfarm animals will run the pytest suites when it is committed?

precedents.title: Revert "Make configure prefer python3 to plain python."

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1 for the missing porting plan, and of standards-compat-2 for the skipped suites. Its claim that the two-framework cost has no recorded answer is also inaccurate, because messages #54, #55, #68 and #90 discuss it.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The shared Python package wraps libpq in a hand-written ctypes binding that depends on the libpq ABI.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: pytest and cryptography are third-party packages on developer and buildfarm machines; message #1 leaves supply-chain safety open.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: A test ported to Python differs from the Perl version on back branches, and version ranges need care on old branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a second test framework, a pgtap plugin, cluster fixtures, and --enable-pytest and -Dpytest build options.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How will buildfarm animals install pytest and cryptography and collect pytest results under both Meson and Autoconf, and does that need a buildfarm client release first?
Until pytest is required, will the Perl version of a ported test stay, so that builds without pytest keep that coverage?
Which Perl suites will be ported, in what order, and what rule decides whether a new test is written in Perl or Python until then?
Which minimum Python, pytest and cryptography versions will each supported branch accept, and who widens the range on old branches?
How do packagers get pytest and cryptography without a virtualenv, the concern Andres Freund raised?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund takes part in the visible thread and supports moving off Perl, but no committer has said they will commit it. The owner must know the build system, the test infrastructure and the buildfarm client.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a second test framework on every supported branch for years: the build options, the pgtap plugin, the cluster fixtures, the libpq binding, and buildfarm failures caused by Python package versions.
committability.author_follow_up: Good sign: Jelte Fennema-Nio cut the patch set down in v9 and rebased it through v13, and both authors have kept the entry active over six CommitFests.

priority.reason: Those who gain are developers who write tests, and several asked for this independently in the thread. The patch touches configure, Meson, CI and a new Python package, and the buildfarm and migration plans are still missing after 116 messages.

provisional_note: Only the v1 and v2 patch prose was read, and the thread is at v13, so the current dependency handling and the Autoconf result path could not be checked. The quality of the fixtures, the libpq binding and the pgtap plugin was not judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rewriting the test of pg_upgrade as a TAP test - take three
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_upgrade's test.sh with a TAP test built on PostgresNode, and drop the upgrade support in the MSVC scripts. The test can upgrade from an older installation, set up either by running pg_regress from the old source tree or by loading a dump of the old cluster.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Open items remained when they end: MSVC support (vcregress.pl) was not done, PostgresNode still needed backward compatibility work, and Michael Paquier wanted the separate SQL file proposal handled first. His last question, whether removing test.sh and requiring TAP was acceptable, has no visible answer.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set replaces pg_upgrade's test.sh with a TAP test and adds cross-version upgrade testing through oldsrc, oldbindir and oldlibdir variables. It refactors PostgresNode.pm so each node records its own binary directory, which get_new_node can set.
precedents_retrieved.objection: A new TAP suite in the pg_upgrade directory would make the buildfarm client run the pg_upgrade tests twice, so a buildfarm client release was needed first, and the author judged the commitfest window too short for v11. Peter Eisentraut also found the PostgresNode.pm bindir refactoring too invasive, because every program call must now observe the bindir setting and future code can forget it. Cross-version runs still failed to load regress.so and related libraries after the upgrade.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Basically, it imposes that from now on all program invocations must observe the bindir setting, which someone is surely going to forget.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support migration of plpythonu to Python 3
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed a configure option that builds a stub plpython2.so on Python-3-only installs, so existing plpythonu functions survive dump/reload and pg_upgrade. The stub redirects plpythonu functions to plpython3 and raises errors for plpython2u functions, and a separate extension converts function bodies with 2to3.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took up the final patch set. Andrew Dunstan helped fix the MSVC build, and Jesse Zhang and Peter Eisentraut questioned parts of the design early on. In the last visible message Tom Lane asks for a review, and the entry was withdrawn a few days later. The visible messages do not show why it was withdrawn rather than left open.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Ping?  I wish somebody would review this.

precedents_retrieved.title: TAP test module - PostgresClient
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Michael Paquier, Peter Eisentraut, Craig Ringer, Andrew Dunstan
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add two Perl modules, PostgresClient and PgResult, under src/test/perl that implement a small frontend-protocol client in Perl so TAP tests can keep interactive sessions open. A postgres_fdw reconnection test was included as an example of its use.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers preferred making psql under IPC::Run usable for such tests, including on Windows, over adding a new test-only client. The patch saw no progress after January, and at commitfest close Andres Freund judged it needed major work to reach agreement. Peter Eisentraut found no explanation of what problem it solves that the existing infrastructure cannot.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I haven't seen any explanation for a problem this is solving.  The
original submission contained a sample test case, by I don't see why
that couldn't be done with the existing infrastructure.

precedents_retrieved.title: Backport perl tests for pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Backport the Perl TAP version of the pg_upgrade tests (commit 322becb60) and related follow-up commits to REL_13_STABLE and REL_14_STABLE, replacing test.sh there. The goal was zero dump differences in cross-version upgrade tests, so users would not need to compare dumps by eye.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the TAP tests were new development that took several tries to get right on HEAD, so backporting them risks a test bug that hides a critical pg_upgrade issue. He preferred to keep further work on HEAD only, and the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If we were to backport
any of this, there is a risk of introducing a bug in what we do with
any of that, potentially hiding a issue critical related to
pg_upgrade.  That's not worth taking a risk for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add ssl_protocols configuration option
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal added an ssl_protocols server GUC, with syntax modeled on Apache's SSLProtocol directive, that controls which SSL/TLS protocol versions the server accepts; its default matches the existing hardcoded behavior. During review the patch was extended with a matching sslprotocol libpq connection option and a shared option parser for client and server.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stalled with no consensus on whether the option was wanted. Michael Paquier noted arguments both for and against it and that the arguments had not changed during the commitfest. He marked it rejected because he was unsure where the discussion was going and whether anyone cared much about the patch. Text quoted in message #16 shows earlier objections that such a GUC re-fights the last war and could be misused to decrease security, but the message containing them is not shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert to using --enable-auto-import in Cygwin builds.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert to using --enable-auto-import in Cygwin builds.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Disabling auto-import requires that all libraries we use be careful about
declspecs for exported variables; and it seems they aren't.  This means
that Cygwin will not give us useful info about missing PGDLLIMPORT markers;
but it's probably sufficient that MSVC and Mingw builds do.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent proposes the same idea. The listed rows share only the buildfarm-readiness reason, which is raised above.
There is no SQL, catalog or psql surface, so the standards angle covers only build options, dependencies and buildfarm integration.

The proposal adds test infrastructure only: build options, a pytest runner, Python fixtures and a ctypes libpq binding. It changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol message or extension ABI, so this angle has nothing to object to.

No objection from the security angle. The proposal adds a developer and CI test framework that is not installed or shipped, so it gives no database role new abilities and exposes nothing to users of a running server. Its trust-auth clusters and test listeners follow what the Perl TAP suite already does. The third-party packages (pytest, cryptography) run only on developer, packager and buildfarm machines. Message #1 already names supply-chain review as an open topic, and v9 dropped the automatic .venv detection. What could not be checked without the code: whether mock servers bind only to localhost, and whether temporary socket directories are private to the test user.
Objections raised; no committer has yet said they will own the result.
One objection only. External tools such as testgres serve out-of-tree use and do not replace in-tree infrastructure, so they give no further objection.
Demand from developers is shown by several independent people in the thread, two in-person meetings, and existing pytest suites outside core. The one objection concerns who pays for that demand.
